_meta.presentationSummary: Coins named for Grand Theft Auto VI, which Rockstar Games released on 2026-11-19 (it posted on 2025-11-06 that the game would release on Thursday, November 19, 2026, and on 2026-11-12 that it was one week away). Forty-six coins are members, thirty-nine of them collected; each has GTA, GTA VI or a GTA VI place, character or in-game brand in its name or description: WASTED ("the iconic GTA death screen"), GTA6CAT, GTA Dollars, Ah shit, here we go again., gtacoin (LaunchLab), Macca The Gator ("GTA 6 Mascot"), State of Leonida and The State of Leonida, Peekhole ("a parody of OnlyFans inside GTA 6"), GTA memes, Jason Duval (it says holders earn $TTWO stock, which is not verified here), Rocco, EEAGLE, Doug The Frog, Jason & Lucia (it says it is unofficial), Official Grand Theft Auto VI (nothing shows it is official), GTA Vice Inu, Grand Trench Agency ("not affiliated with any game"), WANTED, Here We Go Again, and Bawsaq and a Vice City Index coin, named for BAWSAQ, the games' fictional stock exchange. On and after release day, coins named for other in-game things joined: five Apocrycoin coins ("Seen in game overheard on a boat mission"; posts of 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-20 say Apocrycoin is a cryptocurrency mentioned in a mission), two Founder coins ("The exchange for GTA VI crypto"; posts say they started from a "Fundador" badge seen in a DacityCoin screenshot), buckme and BuckMe Coin ("the Cash App of GTA 6"), named for BuckMe, the bank app posts call GTA VI's parody of Cash App (the buckme pool opened on 2026-10-08), PIPI ("PIPI the first meme coin in GTA found"; posts dispute whether an in-game PIPI ad is real), two Cool Dog coins ("the dog that saves every player in GTA6"; "Loosy, jet-ski dog in GTA VI"), and with them GTA Season, VICE 6 ("Vice VI | November 19"), OFFICIALGTA (Jason and Lucia; nothing shows it is official), Hugh Johnson ("one of the standout recurring memes of GTA VI's Snapmatic world") and Grand Theft Crew (StonkFun; "a GTA-inspired memecoin"). Of the collected coins, all but gtacoin (LaunchLab), Grand Theft Crew (StonkFun) and one apocrycoin (Meteora DBC) are on Pump.fun. Dates from Codex: the GTA6CAT and GTA memes pools opened in late August 2026, buckme and several others in October, VICE 6 on 2026-11-13 and most others between 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-20, so most launched ahead of the release on its hype. Archived (under $1,000 of 24h volume on two consecutive observations; memberships stay open): Mission Passed, GRAND THEFT CRYPTO, Cyber Dacity Coin, Vice City Bawsaq, the Meteora DBC Vice City Index, Leonida Games and Grand Theft Anthropic. Coins named for the in-game DacityCoin/AudaCity brand are a separate narrative (GTA 6 Dacity Coin coins). The in-game references are as posts describe them and were not checked here; none of the coins is shown to be connected to Rockstar Games or Take-Two.

title: GTA 6 Dacity Coin coins
summary: Coins named for Dacity Coin, an in-game meme coin that posts say appears in GTA 6 material. On 2026-10-11 the account @robtmb1 (RobTheMaster) posted that there is a meme coin in GTA 6 called "Dacity Coin" in a new leak (e4:0); the first Dacity Coin on pump.fun was created 35 seconds later (token created 2026-10-11 11:16 UTC, post at 11:15 UTC). A post of 2026-10-19 from the GTA 6 Intel account says DacityCoin appears on a stunt plane in GTA VI's launch trailer, a fictional crypto brand parodying real meme coins (e4:1). An automated claim check rated the claim "partly real" on 2026-10-18, saying the Dacity Coin name in GTA 6 material is real and widely reported but the leak timestamp and the leak's authenticity were not verified, and an earlier check on 2026-10-15 called it unclear (e4:0). Four coins carry the name: Dacity Coin (pump.fun, Solana; token created 2026-10-11), AudaCity (pump.fun; token created 2026-10-15 13:22 UTC), Dacity Coin (Pons, Robinhood Chain; created 2026-10-19 16:13 UTC) and GTAVI AudaCity (pump.fun; created 2026-10-20 04:04 UTC), whose metadata repeats the claim: "There's a meme coin in GTA 6 called \"Dacity Coin\" in the new leak." The other three have empty metadata, so their names carry the claim. Most posts about the coins are call-group promotion and listing-vote spam, and none of the coins is shown to be affiliated with Rockstar, Take-Two or the leak. These are traders' and the coins' own claims. Measured: four coins across all their pools.
